correctness.rationale: Independently enumerated all 1037 nonempty simplices of the ordinary matching complex of the explicit 18-edge GP(6,2), obtaining face counts (18,117,334,402,156,10). Independently generated all 506 greedy Morse pairs and 3684 Hasse covers, topologically sorted all 1037 directed nodes, and performed 506 integral unit-pivot chain cancellations in reverse-pair order, leaving a primitive boundary supported on exactly two 3-cells. This confirms the already-published integral wedge of 22 S3. For each of all 12 D6 automorphisms an independently implemented oriented fixed-simplex Lefschetz sum gives rotation third-homology traces (22,0,-2,6,-2,0) and six reflection traces zero. Exact character inner products give one-dimensional multiplicities 2,2,1,1 and 2-dimensional multiplicities 3,5. The resulting representation dimension is 22 and full invariant subspace dimension two. Graph automorphisms are exactly D6: the outer cycle is distinguished by no triangle, and the six spokes uniquely extend the cycle symmetries. All claimed numerical and topological boundaries refer only to this finite fixed graph; finite exhaustive enumeration is a proof for that graph. The complete original ten-file Git tree was reconstructed independently from the actual Git blob SHA listing and matches the assigned tree SHA.
residual_risks: The homotopy equivalence is already prior art; the revised mathematical result is only the rational D6 character.
A finite signed Lefschetz computation proves the fixed graph but does not determine the integral D6 representation lattice or equivariant homotopy type.

value.rationale: The full group character is a natural invariant of a canonical cubic polyhedral graph, refining a known 22-dimensional homology rank by distinguishing six irreducible constituent multiplicities and a two-dimensional invariant subspace. This precise orientation-sensitive action is useful for further equivariant topology; no family theorem is claimed.
residual_risks: A single-graph character is a limited exact invariant, not a general-family theorem.
The previously published stronger octahedral carrier and lattice classification reduces the independence of the homotopy portion, which is excluded from the final novelty claim.

scientific_limitations: The 22-sphere homotopy theorem is exactly covered by an earlier October 18 publication; the original combined statement cannot pass as a fresh homotopy theorem.
The corrected claim singles out the D6 rational character, which is verified for this finite graph, not an integer representation-lattice or graph-family classification.
Originality is best-of-knowledge; the signed dihedral character might appear in unindexed prior sources or be derivable from published signed-carrier datasets.
